hook: TO DRIVE HERE|FROM THE US, YOU|GO THROUGH CANADA

beats.say: To drive to this part of Minnesota, you have to go through Canada first.
It's the Northwest Angle. The only piece of the lower 48 states north of the 49th parallel.
Blame a bad map. In 1783, the treaty that ended the American Revolution drew the border through the Lake of the Woods.
The negotiators used the Mitchell Map. It got the lake and the Mississippi's source wrong.
When surveyors finally fixed the line, this little corner ended up cut off, with the lake on one side and Canada on the other.
About 150 people live there. And to enter, they check in at a kiosk instead of a border guard.
The other options? A boat, a plane, or in winter, a road built on the frozen lake. Would you live there?

yt.description:
The Northwest Angle, Minnesota: the only part of the contiguous US north of the 49th parallel, reachable by land only through Manitoba. A 1783 treaty drew the border through Lake of the Woods using the faulty Mitchell Map; 149 people lived there in 2020.
